reviewed_protocol.prepare: web.read.prepare({}) allocates a same-owner one-shot read_id with process scope and 120000 ms retention
reviewed_protocol.read: web.read optionally accepts read_id; named and legacy reads use distinct shared-flight identities
reviewed_protocol.cancel: web.read.cancel({read_id}) cancels one member; the last active member closes admission before Worker cooperation
reviewed_protocol.worker: fetch.extract_direct with independent control_id; fetch.cancel_direct never enters the durable grant namespace

required_properties: Claim a prepared read_id atomically before any profile or network work; one handle cannot authorize two reads.
A prepared cancellation prevents later dispatch; same-owner lookup is required and foreign/absent handles must not leak ownership.
Use steady-clock retention; do not expire running members; repeated control does not refresh terminal retention; capacity rejects rather than evicts live state or unexpired tombstones.
No automatic fallback or re-dispatch if the direct-specific Worker method is unsupported or its reply is lost; legacy calls keep their existing Worker parameters.
Cumulative membership remains bounded at 32; cancelled and timed-out members do not free cumulative admission slots.
Count active members separately; last-member removal and admission closure share one coordination-lock linearization point.
Do not hold the coordination lock during Store calls or Worker RPC, and never introduce detached physical-execution threads.
The fixed payer remains the accounting owner after cancellation; subscribers never inherit the physical charge.
A subscriber cancelling before physical settlement returns known-zero incremental usage and unknown associated physical usage, not a fabricated zero physical attempt.
All completion, error, timeout and cancellation exits retire their claimed member exactly once and cannot leave a permanently running handle.
After the Store window is ready, success delivery must race cancellation through a final coordinated transition; cancellation winning that transition prevents the member receiving body content.
Core final principal-revocation checks should preserve already-known execution usage without releasing the body.
Direct control preserves 60000 ms public timeouts, ordinary redirect-body accounting, truncation and output-window semantics; it does not instantiate FetchBudget.

Worker cancellation is checked before outbound dispatch, after host-slot waits, before subsequent redirects, during streaming, and after extraction yields; cancelled outputs retain reliable usage and valid restrictive observations.
Worker direct active/retired control identities are separate from durable attempts, bounded, and preserve cancel-before-start and replay protection within their documented retention window.
explicit_scope_limits_required: Payer control can acknowledge immediately while the original synchronous read waits for bounded physical settlement; do not promise immediate termination of that read call.

Without holding a coordination lock across Store ingestion or a persistent cancellation fence, cancellation cannot retroactively roll back a commit that has already begun. Document the exact submission versus delivery boundary.
The existing HTTP business pool may return E_REQUEST_BACKPRESSURE to cancellation when full; no arbitrary-load immediate-cancel guarantee follows from the API.
Process-scoped handles and Worker tombstones are not a persistent execution or budget journal and do not establish restart recovery, no-charge execution or safe automatic retries.
Cross-WebService, cross-process and cross-channel sharing remain out of scope; complete B-24 and CACHE-01 acceptance remains unsigned.
next_review: Inspect implementation and independently exercise member races, preserved direct contracts, Worker cancellation accounting, HTTP/MCP transport, and final execution-input binding.
